channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Karnataka women's group wins national award for saving indigenous seeds [7/10]
item.description: A self-help group of women farmers in Dharwad won a national award and ten lakh rupees for conserving more than 250 indigenous seed varieties. (Goodness 7/10: Protects crop diversity and recognises local farmers.)

item.title: Drug baxdrostat reverses hormone-driven high blood pressure in study [7/10]
item.description: A study of the FDA-approved drug baxdrostat found it reversed high blood pressure caused by excess hormone production in patients with the condition. (Goodness 7/10: Promising results for a common, hard-to-treat condition, though from a single study.)

item.title: Children's Hospital of New Orleans opens museum inside the hospital [6/10]
item.description: A young patient wanted a place for play and fresh air during treatment, and the hospital built a museum space for children to be distracted and enjoy time outdoors. (Goodness 6/10: A kind, local initiative that helps children in care.)

item.title: Assam village shifts from chasing elephants to feeding and mapping them [7/10]
item.description: Residents of Hatikhuli village in Assam changed their approach to wild elephants, feeding them and mapping their movements rather than driving them away. (Goodness 7/10: A community-led approach to coexistence with wildlife.)

item.title: IIT Roorkee team creates new spring to double village drinking water [7/10]
item.description: Researchers from IIT Roorkee located underground water and created a new spring in Unchaun village, Uttarakhand, raising drinking water supply in the lean season. (Goodness 7/10: Tangible water access for a village, and a method others could copy.)

item.title: Zimbabwean author cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story [6/10]
item.description: After a month-long investigation, Simbarashe Kundizeza's prize-winning entry was found to have been written by a human. (Goodness 6/10: A good outcome for one writer.)

item.title: Drone-collected whale breath yields a full genome [7/10]
item.description: Researchers used a drone to gather exhaled breath from a whale and sequenced a complete genome from it, avoiding the need for invasive sampling. (Goodness 7/10: A non-invasive method that could make wildlife genetics research easier on animals.)

item.title: One-time CRISPR therapy cuts bad cholesterol by about half in early trial [6/10]
item.description: A Phase 1 trial at Cleveland Clinic found a single infusion of a CRISPR gene-editing therapy lowered harmful cholesterol by roughly 50%. (Goodness 6/10: Promising result, but it is an early human trial with a small group.)

item.title: Lundy Island shows results of decades of conservation [7/10]
item.description: A video report describes how long-running conservation on Lundy Island in the Bristol Channel has brought wildlife back. (Goodness 7/10: Long-term protection delivering visible recovery.)

item.title: X-ray telescope bound for Mercury makes first observations [6/10]
item.description: After eight years in space, an X-ray telescope on its way to Mercury has made its first cosmic observations and is working well. (Goodness 6/10: A scientific milestone, with limited direct benefit to daily life.)

item.title: Michigan net-zero community to become state's first virtual power plant [6/10]
item.description: Homes in the Veridian development in Ann Arbor will join a DTE Energy pilot that lets the utility draw on residential energy resources to support the grid. (Goodness 6/10: A useful pilot for clean, flexible power, still small in scale.)

item.title: French police officers jailed for assaulting Black music producer [6/10]
item.description: A French court sentenced three officers to five years in prison, partly suspended, and treated racism as an aggravating factor in the assault. (Goodness 6/10: Accountability for police violence, though the case itself is a harm.)

item.title: Quechua community in Peru runs its own Andean bear camera-trap project [7/10]
item.description: The Quechua community of Pillco Grande uses camera traps on its reserve in Pumataki to study Andean bears. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led monitoring supports protection of a vulnerable species.)

item.title: Community replaces teen landscaper's stolen equipment [6/10]
item.description: After about $20,000 of landscaping gear was stolen from a teenage business owner in Kansas, local people stepped in to replace it. (Goodness 6/10: A local act of kindness that helps one young entrepreneur.)

item.title: Japan begins commercial offshore wind power [6/10]
item.description: Japan's offshore wind sector has started commercial operations with about 0.5 GW online, though hurdles to expansion remain. (Goodness 6/10: Real clean energy progress, still small and facing obstacles.)

item.title: Floating wind gains momentum toward commercial scale [6/10]
item.description: Floating turbines, which work in deep water, remain at small demonstration scale but industry momentum toward commercialization is growing. (Goodness 6/10: Promising technology that is not yet widely deployed.)

item.title: Young researchers win $15,000 for Tamiraparani river work [6/10]
item.description: A team studying a 30-km stretch of Tamil Nadu's Tamiraparani river won a $15,000 grant for community-based monitoring of a river facing pollution. (Goodness 6/10: Recognition and funding for river protection, with pollution still a problem.)

item.title: Family business makes paper from rhino dung in India [7/10]
item.description: A father and daughter in India turn rhino dung collected by villagers into paper and stationery, giving locals steady income and a reason to protect the animals. (Goodness 7/10: Local income tied directly to rhino protection, though on a small scale.)

item.title: Trout raised on an all-algae diet could reduce wild fish use in farming [7/10]
item.description: Researchers fed farmed rainbow trout a diet made entirely of two marine microalgae, pointing to a way to stop using wild fish as feed. (Goodness 7/10: Promising for ocean health, but still a research result.)

item.title: Toronto-area chef cooks weekly meals for 100 people in need [6/10]
item.description: Chef Maddy Goldberg volunteers every Tuesday, preparing meals for 100 people from whatever ingredients a local food bank has available. (Goodness 6/10: A reliable community kindness that helps many neighbours.)

item.title: CERN finds first evidence of extremely rare particle decay [6/10]
item.description: Researchers at CERN found first evidence of a particle decay expected only about once in every 10 billion beauty particles, after a roughly 40-year search. (Goodness 6/10: A scientific milestone, with no direct benefit to people yet.)

item.title: Montreal park uses ocean sounds to soften traffic noise [6/10]
item.description: A Montreal park now plays recorded coastal sounds to make the space calmer beside busy roads. The project draws on Magdalen Islands heritage and has been made permanent. (Goodness 6/10: A low-cost urban comfort fix, local in reach.)

item.title: Indigenous Philippine farmers investigate farming and soil erosion link [6/10]
item.description: T'boli farmers in Lake Sebu, Mindanao, with NGO and scientific support, are testing whether chemical farming contributes to soil erosion. (Goodness 6/10: Community-led research with practical potential.)

item.title: Zimbabwe has destroyed 250,000 landmines since 2013 [8/10]
item.description: The HALO Trust says it has cleared 250,000 landmines in Zimbabwe since 2013, but warns that funding shortfalls threaten the goal of finishing by 2030. (Goodness 8/10: Large safety gain for communities, with the finish line at risk.)

item.title: Deaf Nigerians work to preserve indigenous sign languages [6/10]
item.description: Deaf people in Nigeria are working to keep indigenous sign languages alive, with Hausa sign serving as a common language in the north and central to their identity. (Goodness 6/10: Cultural preservation effort by a community, modest in scale.)

item.title: Neighbor's check-in leads strangers to raise over $109,000 for woman, 87 [7/10]
item.description: After a neighbor checked on a noisy upstairs resident, strangers raised more than $109,000 for Carole, 87, who lives alone with Parkinson's disease. (Goodness 7/10: Direct, lasting help for one person and an inspiring act of community.)

item.title: Indian research turns paddy straw into a mushroom growing medium [7/10]
item.description: ICAR-NRRI research shows rice straw can be used to grow mushrooms, offering an alternative use for crop stubble. (Goodness 7/10: Practical idea that could cut stubble burning and add farm income.)

item.title: Voyager 1 passes one light-day from Earth [6/10]
item.description: The Empire State Building was lit gold to mark Voyager 1 reaching a distance of one light-day from Earth, a milestone for the long-running NASA mission. (Goodness 6/10: A space-exploration milestone with little direct impact on lives.)

item.title: Old wind turbine blades turned into stronger new material [6/10]
item.description: Tsinghua University researchers used flash heating to convert ground blade waste into silicon carbide and graphene, which made new epoxy resin stiffer and stronger. (Goodness 6/10: Promising answer to wind blade waste, still at lab stage.)

item.title: Lundy island profiled as a conservation success [7/10]
item.description: A video feature looks at Lundy, a small island in the Bristol Channel between Wales and England, and the conservation results achieved there. (Goodness 7/10: A local conservation success that offers a model for others.)

item.title: IIT Bombay startup's AI monitor has screened 1 million pregnancies in India [8/10]
item.description: A startup born at IIT Bombay has screened one million pregnancies across India with AI-powered fetal and labour monitoring devices. (Goodness 8/10: Wide reach in maternal healthcare in India.)

item.title: Over 100 cave bear skeletons found in an Alpine cave [6/10]
item.description: Authorities revealed a cave holding more than 100 extinct cave bear skeletons, found by a mountain guide and kept secret to protect the site. (Goodness 6/10: A notable scientific find protected from looting.)

item.title: Earthshot Prize 2026 winners announced [7/10]
item.description: The 2026 Earthshot Prize winners were announced, and for the first time research on positive tipping points helped shape the selection. (Goodness 7/10: Recognition for environmental solutions, but a prize rather than delivered impact.)

item.title: Washing machines that clean clothes with liquid carbon dioxide [7/10]
item.description: Liquid carbon dioxide under pressure can clean fabrics without water or dryer heat, and manufacturers are developing machines that use it. (Goodness 7/10: Promising water and energy savings, but still early in adoption.)

item.title: Giant anteaters return to parts of their former range [7/10]
item.description: Habitat restoration and rewilding are bringing vulnerable giant anteaters back to areas they left; one was recorded in Argentina's Alma Guaraní reserve in 2025, the first there since 1986. (Goodness 7/10: Real recovery for a vulnerable species, still in limited areas.)

item.title: Borneo Indigenous groups mark land-rights victory with memorial stone [7/10]
item.description: Berawan, Penan and Tering communities in Malaysian Borneo placed a memorial stone marking their land-rights win and as a message to future generations. (Goodness 7/10: A legal win for communities, tempered by continuing pressures.)

item.title: Tunisia's olive oil exports jump nearly 50% after bumper harvest [6/10]
item.description: Tunisia's olive oil exports rose by nearly 50% on a bumper harvest, boosting income for the sector. (Goodness 6/10: Economic gain for producers, tied to one good harvest.)

item.title: Students work to save a plant found only near their campus [6/10]
item.description: Santa Clara University scientists are protecting the Santa Clara Valley liveforever, a rare succulent threatened by poaching. (Goodness 6/10: Local conservation effort protecting a very rare plant.)

item.title: Siblings hand-build 430-step staircase for their mother in China [6/10]
item.description: The children of an elderly Chinese mother built a staircase up a mountainside so she could keep living in her home rather than move to the city. (Goodness 6/10: A heartwarming family story with local impact.)

item.title: Antarctic blue whale population grows about tenfold since whaling ended [8/10]
item.description: Antarctic blue whales rose from 418 individuals in 1973 to roughly 4,018, growing about 4.5% a year after commercial whaling stopped. (Goodness 8/10: Clear recovery of a once-nearly-extinct species, though numbers remain small.)

item.title: Study maps jaguar habitat links across the Americas [6/10]
item.description: A Global Change Biology study assesses habitat connectivity for jaguars across the Americas to guide efforts to help populations recover. (Goodness 6/10: Useful planning tool for conservation; results depend on follow-up action.)

item.title: Thirty-year study links acorn years to Lyme disease risk [6/10]
item.description: A 30-year study in New York forests finds surges in deer tick numbers follow mouse booms triggered by heavy acorn crops, helping predict Lyme risk. (Goodness 6/10: Better prediction can help prevent disease, though it is research rather than a cure.)

item.title: Two women turn burnt crop straw into a business [7/10]
item.description: Founders from Haryana and Rajasthan started SSAR Biomass Green, turning farm straw that is often burned into useful products. (Goodness 7/10: Reduces burning and pollution while creating income.)

item.title: India wins 10th SAFF football title with a second-string squad [6/10]
item.description: India beat Pakistan to claim its tenth SAFF Championship title without its star players. (Goodness 6/10: Sporting success and community pride.)

item.title: Lucio Usobiaga wins Basque Culinary World Prize for protecting Mexico's chinampas [7/10]
item.description: Usobiaga won the 2026 Basque Culinary World Prize for Arca Tierra, a network supporting farmers who maintain Mexico's chinampa ecosystem. (Goodness 7/10: Recognition and support for traditional, sustainable farming.)

item.title: Rescued olive ridley sea turtle hatchlings released into the Pacific [6/10]
item.description: Olive ridley hatchlings rescued ahead of a California storm were released into the Pacific, described as the first such release on the US West Coast. (Goodness 6/10: A small but hopeful rescue of a threatened species.)

item.title: Earthshot Prize winners honoured in Mumbai [6/10]
item.description: Prince William presented five Earthshot Prize winners with one million pounds each for environmental solutions at a ceremony in Mumbai. (Goodness 6/10: Funding boosts proven environmental projects.)

item.title: Fela Kuti becomes first African inducted into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame [7/10]
item.description: The Nigerian Afrobeat pioneer has been inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the first African artist to receive the honour. (Goodness 7/10: A landmark recognition for African music.)

item.title: Scimitar-horned oryx returns to Chad [8/10]
item.description: A reintroduction programme led by Sahara Conservation has rebuilt a wild population of the scimitar-horned oryx in Chad. (Goodness 8/10: Successful return of a species once extinct in the wild.)

item.title: Algeria repays hospitality shown to its World Cup team by Kansans [6/10]
item.description: Kansans visiting Algeria were greeted at 4:30 a.m. with flowers by officials and hospitality workers, repaying the welcome Kansas gave Algeria's World Cup team. (Goodness 6/10: A warm goodwill gesture between communities.)

item.title: Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion in shares ahead of Thanksgiving [7/10]
item.description: Warren Buffett converted Berkshire Hathaway shares into a $5.5 billion gift for charitable foundations, saying kindness is important. (Goodness 7/10: Large donation helping many causes.)

item.title: New York's largest electric school bus fleet serves a South Bronx neighborhood [7/10]
item.description: The largest electric school bus fleet in New York State now runs in a South Bronx neighborhood with high childhood asthma rates, cutting exposure to diesel exhaust. (Goodness 7/10: Cleaner air for children in a high-asthma area.)

item.title: Rewari revives 10 ponds to store water as groundwater falls [7/10]
item.description: TERI and Nokia India are restoring 10 village ponds in Haryana's Rewari district over 24 months, aiming to store 120 million litres of water. (Goodness 7/10: Practical local water security, though results are still to come.)

item.title: Indian startup turns crop stubble into biochar [7/10]
item.description: Takachar, an Earthshot Awards winner, uses portable equipment to convert crop stubble into biochar, offering farmers an alternative to burning. (Goodness 7/10: Could cut field-burning smoke, if it scales.)

item.title: African artists take four of five global album spots in 2027 Grammy nominations [6/10]
item.description: African musicians received four of the five nominations in the Grammy global music album category. (Goodness 6/10: Wider recognition of African music.)

item.title: Proposed marine protected area could safeguard whale sharks in Indonesia [6/10]
item.description: Plans for a marine protected area in Indonesia's Saleh Bay would cover important habitat for whale sharks. (Goodness 6/10: Still a plan, not yet in force.)

item.title: Somerset volunteers take on the perspectives of local wildlife [6/10]
item.description: Volunteers in the River Tone catchment in Somerset took on the viewpoints of animals such as kestrels to rethink how the landscape is managed. (Goodness 6/10: A creative community approach to nature recovery.)

item.title: AIIMS Delhi performs open foetal surgery at 25 weeks [7/10]
item.description: Surgeons at AIIMS Delhi repaired myelomeningocele, a spinal defect, in a baby before birth at 25 weeks of pregnancy. (Goodness 7/10: A medical milestone, though for a small number of patients.)

item.title: Japanese town uses rice paddies to hold floodwater [7/10]
item.description: Osaki has installed more than 5,000 small earthen dams in surrounding rice paddies so the fields can hold floodwater and reduce flooding. (Goodness 7/10: Low-cost climate adaptation using existing farmland.)

item.title: Forever chemicals fall in English rivers and fish [7/10]
item.description: Two internationally restricted PFAS chemicals have dropped about 30% in English river water and 49% in fish, according to a BBC report. (Goodness 7/10: Restrictions are visibly working, though the chemicals persist.)
